summary: tailnet ingress: Caddy listener split + Tailscale cert renewal timer
description:
deploy/Caddyfile gains a tailnet listener bound to guru-web-prod.<tailnet>.ts.net.  Public listener gains @admin matcher rewriting to /_admin-404 (so the rejection page shape matches a normal Next 404).  Tailscale cert renewal happens out-of-band via a daily systemd timer running 'tailscale cert' to disk; Caddy reads files like any other TLS pair.  See BRD-admin-ui.md §0.1 + §0.3.

Files:
  - deploy/Caddyfile  (edit)
  - deploy/tailnet-cert-renew.sh  (new)
  - deploy/tailnet-cert-renew.service  (new, oneshot)
  - deploy/tailnet-cert-renew.timer  (new, daily)
  - deploy/README.md  (new 'Tailnet admin listener' install + recovery procedures)

deploy/vps-bootstrap.sh stays untouched — bootstrap is one-shot, admin install is a deliberate hand-patch.

Done when:
  - 'caddy validate' passes locally and on VPS.
  - curl https://guru-ai.org/admin/ → Next-style 404 (not bare Caddy 404).
  - curl https://guru-web-prod.<tailnet>.ts.net/admin/ from a tailnet device reaches Next.js (will 404 the empty admin route until 6cedb4d0 lands).
  - systemctl list-timers shows tailnet-cert-renew.timer active.
  - Manual /usr/local/bin/tailnet-cert-renew regenerates files + reloads Caddy.

Tests: manual smoke (curl + systemctl) — documented in deploy/README.md.  No unit-test surface; see IMPL §1.

Operator action post-merge: copy Caddyfile + units onto the VPS, validate, reload caddy, install timer.  Sequence in deploy/README.md.
